title: Hablar de experiencias pasadas / Talking about past experiences
bridge: In Spanish we say 'cuando era niño...' or 'antes yo...' to talk about the past. In French we use the imparfait for past habits or states (Quand j'étais enfant..., Avant je...) and the passé composé for specific events (Une fois j'ai...).
rule: Use the imparfait (imperfect) to describe how things were or what you habitually did in the past. Use the passé composé to tell something that happened once or at a specific moment. The phrase 'une fois' (once) always goes with the passé composé.

concept_examples.text: Quand j'étais enfant, j'habitais à la campagne.
concept_examples.translation: When I was a child, I lived in the countryside.
concept_examples.phonetic: /kɑ̃ ʒetɛ ɑ̃fɑ̃, ʒabitɛ a la kɑ̃paɲ/

concept_examples.text: Avant, je prenais le bus tous les jours.
concept_examples.translation: Before, I took the bus every day.
concept_examples.phonetic: /avɑ̃, ʒə pʁənɛ lə bys tu lɛ ʒuʁ/

concept_examples.text: Une fois, j'ai rencontré une star.
concept_examples.translation: Once, I met a movie star.

common_error.wrong: Quand j'étais enfant, j'ai joué au foot tous les weekends.
common_error.correct: Quand j'étais enfant, je jouais au foot tous les weekends.
common_error.explanation: When you describe a habitual or repeated action in the past, you must use the imparfait (je jouais), not the passé composé (j'ai joué). The passé composé is reserved for unique actions or those that happened at a specific moment.

examples.original: Quand j'étais petit, j'aimais les bonbons.
examples.phonetic: /kɑ̃ ʒetɛ pəti, ʒemɛ lɛ bɔ̃bɔ̃/
examples.translation: When I was little, I liked candies.
examples.note: Basic structure: Quand j'étais + adjective + imparfait.

examples.original: Avant, je dormais beaucoup.
examples.phonetic: /avɑ̃, ʒə dɔʁmɛ boku/
examples.translation: Before, I slept a lot.
examples.note: 'Avant' at the beginning of the sentence signals contrast with the present.

examples.original: Une fois, j'ai oublié mon sac à l'école.
examples.phonetic: /yn fwa, ʒɛ ublje mɔ̃ sak a lekɔl/
examples.translation: Once, I forgot my backpack at school.
examples.note: 'Une fois' introduces a specific event: always with passé composé.

examples.original: Avant, on habitait dans un grand appartement.
examples.phonetic: /avɑ̃, ɔ̃ nabitɛ dɑ̃z‿œ̃ ɡʁɑ̃ t‿apaʁtəmɑ̃/
examples.translation: Before, we lived in a big apartment.
examples.note: 'On' is equivalent to 'we' in informal context.

examples.original: Quand j'étais adolescent, j'ai commencé à apprendre la guitare.
examples.phonetic: /kɑ̃ ʒetɛ adɔlesɑ̃, ʒɛ kɔmɑ̃se a apʁɑ̃dʁ la ɡitaʁ/
examples.translation: When I was a teenager, I started learning the guitar.
examples.note: The imparfait describes the context (adolescence), the passé composé the specific event (starting).

examples.original: Avant, je n'aimais pas les légumes, mais une fois j'ai goûté des courgettes et j'ai adoré.
examples.phonetic: /avɑ̃, ʒə nemɛ pa lɛ leɡym, mɛ yn fwa ʒɛ ɡute dɛ kuʁʒɛt e ʒɛ adɔʁe/
examples.translation: Before, I didn't like vegetables, but once I tried zucchini and I loved them.
examples.note: Advanced example combining avant + imparfait and une fois + passé composé.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Tu te souviens de ton enfance ?
dialogue.translation: Do you remember your childhood?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Oui ! Quand j'étais enfant, j'habitais à la mer.
dialogue.translation: Yes! When I was a child, I lived by the sea.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: C'est sympa ! Et une fois, quelque chose d'extraordinaire t'est arrivé ?
dialogue.translation: That's nice! And once, did something extraordinary happen to you?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Oui, une fois j'ai vu un dauphin depuis la plage !
dialogue.translation: Yes, once I saw a dolphin from the beach!

title: Hacer planes y citas / Making plans and appointments
bridge: To meet up with someone in French, we use expressions like 'On se retrouve à...' (let's meet at...), 'Je serai là à...' (I'll be there at...) and 'Tu es libre...?' (Are you free...?). The future simple (futur simple) or the construction aller + infinitive express plans.
rule: To propose a meeting, use 'On se retrouve + place/time'. To confirm your availability, use 'Je serai là à + time' (futur simple of être). To ask if someone is free, use 'Tu es libre + day/time ?' The construction 'aller + infinitive' (je vais venir) also expresses immediate plans.

concept_examples.text: On se retrouve à la gare à dix heures ?
concept_examples.translation: Shall we meet at the station at ten?
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɔ̃ sə ʁətʁuv a la ɡaʁ a dizœʁ/

concept_examples.text: Je serai là à midi pile.
concept_examples.translation: I'll be there at exactly noon.

concept_examples.text: Tu es libre samedi soir ?
concept_examples.translation: Are you free Saturday evening?

common_error.wrong: On se retrouve à dix heures du matin du matin.
common_error.correct: On se retrouve à dix heures du matin.
common_error.correct_alt: On se retrouve à dix heures.
common_error.explanation: Do not repeat 'du matin'. Also, in informal French, it is enough to say the time without 'du matin' if the context is clear. Avoid redundancies.

examples.original: On se retrouve au café ?
examples.phonetic: /ɔ̃ sə ʁətʁuv o kafe/
examples.translation: Shall we meet at the café?
examples.note: 'On se retrouve' is the most natural expression for meeting up in informal French.

examples.original: Tu es libre demain ?
examples.phonetic: /ty ɛ libʁ dəmɛ̃/
examples.translation: Are you free tomorrow?
examples.note: A simple question to check the other person's availability.

examples.original: Je serai là à dix-huit heures devant le cinéma.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə səʁɛ la a dizɥitœʁ dəvɑ̃ lə sinema/
examples.translation: I'll be there at six in the evening in front of the cinema.
examples.note: Future simple of 'être': je serai, tu seras, il/elle sera...

examples.original: On va se retrouver à la brasserie du coin.
examples.phonetic: /ɔ̃ va sə ʁətʁuve a la bʁasʁi dy kwɛ̃/
examples.translation: We're going to meet at the local brasserie.
examples.note: Aller + infinitive expresses a near or agreed plan.

examples.original: Je ne suis pas libre à midi, mais je serai disponible à partir de quatorze heures.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə nə sɥi pa libʁ a midi, mɛ ʒə səʁɛ dispɔnibl a paʁtiʁ də katɔʁzœʁ/
examples.translation: I'm not free at noon, but I'll be available from two o'clock.
examples.note: 'À partir de' means 'from', very useful for negotiating times.

examples.original: Désolé(e), je dois annuler notre rendez-vous. On se retrouve un autre jour ?
examples.phonetic: /dezɔle, ʒə dwa anyle nɔtʁ ʁɑ̃devu. ɔ̃ sə ʁətʁuv œ̃ notʁ ʒuʁ/
examples.translation: Sorry, I have to cancel our appointment. Shall we meet another day?
examples.note: 'Rendez-vous' means appointment or meeting (not just a medical appointment).

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Tu es libre vendredi soir ?
dialogue.translation: Are you free Friday evening?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Oui, pourquoi ?
dialogue.translation: Yes, why?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: On se retrouve au restaurant à vingt heures ?
dialogue.translation: Shall we meet at the restaurant at eight?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Super idée ! Je serai là à vingt heures pile.
dialogue.translation: Great idea! I'll be there at exactly eight.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Parfait, à vendredi !
dialogue.translation: Perfect, see you Friday!

title: Dar consejos y recomendaciones / Giving advice and recommendations
bridge: In Spanish we say 'deberías...', 'habría que...' or 'te aconsejo que...'. In French the equivalent structures are 'Tu devrais + infinitive', 'Il faudrait + infinitive' and 'Je te conseille de + infinitive'. All express advice or recommendation in a polite way.
rule: 'Tu devrais' is the conditional of 'devoir' (must) and is the most direct way to advise. 'Il faudrait' is the impersonal conditional of 'falloir' (to be necessary) and sounds more neutral. 'Je te conseille de' is more personal and friendly. All three are followed by an infinitive.

concept_examples.text: Tu devrais boire plus d'eau.
concept_examples.translation: You should drink more water.

concept_examples.text: Il faudrait parler au médecin.
concept_examples.translation: One should talk to the doctor.

concept_examples.text: Je te conseille de te reposer.
concept_examples.translation: I advise you to rest.

common_error.wrong: Je te conseille que tu te reposes.
common_error.correct: Je te conseille de te reposer.
common_error.explanation: 'Je te conseille' is followed by 'de + infinitive', not 'que + subjunctive'. This is a very common error for Spanish speakers because in Spanish we say 'te aconsejo que descanses' with the subjunctive. In French, the construction is simpler: de + infinitive.

examples.original: Tu devrais dormir plus.
examples.phonetic: /ty dəvʁɛ dɔʁmiʁ plys/
examples.translation: You should sleep more.
examples.note: 'Tu devrais' is the most common and direct way to give personal advice.

examples.original: Il faudrait faire du sport.
examples.phonetic: /il fodʁɛ fɛʁ dy spɔʁ/
examples.translation: One should do sports.
examples.note: 'Il faudrait' is not directed at anyone in particular: it is general advice.

examples.original: Si tu es fatigué, tu devrais prendre un café.
examples.phonetic: /si ty ɛ fatiɡe, ty dəvʁɛ pʁɑ̃dʁ œ̃ kafe/
examples.translation: If you are tired, you should have a coffee.
examples.note: The advice can be preceded by a condition with 'si + present'.

examples.original: Je te conseille de visiter le Louvre, c'est magnifique.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə tə kɔ̃sɛj də vizite lə luvʁ, sɛ maɲifik/
examples.translation: I advise you to visit the Louvre, it's magnificent.
examples.note: You can add a justification after the recommendation to sound more natural.

examples.original: À ta place, je parlerais à ton chef le plus tôt possible.
examples.phonetic: /a ta plas, ʒə paʁləʁɛ a tɔ̃ ʃɛf lə ply to pɔsibl/
examples.translation: In your place, I would talk to your boss as soon as possible.
examples.note: 'À ta place, je + conditional' is a very polite way to give advice, equivalent to 'if I were you...'.

examples.original: Il vaudrait mieux ne pas sortir par ce temps.
examples.phonetic: /il vodʁɛ mjø nə pa sɔʁtiʁ paʁ sə tɑ̃/
examples.translation: It would be better not to go out in this weather.
examples.note: 'Il vaudrait mieux + infinitive' expresses that something is preferable; it is more formal than 'il faudrait'.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: J'ai mal à la tête depuis ce matin.
dialogue.translation: I have a headache since this morning.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Tu devrais boire de l'eau et te reposer un peu.
dialogue.translation: You should drink water and rest a bit.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Tu crois ? Il faudrait aussi prendre un médicament ?
dialogue.translation: You think? Should I also take some medicine?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Je te conseille de parler à un médecin si ça continue.
dialogue.translation: I advise you to talk to a doctor if it continues.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: D'accord, merci pour les conseils !
dialogue.translation: Okay, thanks for the advice!

title: Expresar opiniones / Expressing opinions
bridge: In Spanish we say 'creo que...', 'me parece que...' or 'en mi opinión...'. In French the equivalent structures are 'Je pense que...', 'Je trouve que...', 'À mon avis...' and 'Il me semble que...'. They all serve to express what you think or feel about something.
rule: 'Je pense que' and 'Je trouve que' are followed by a complete sentence with subject + verb in the indicative. 'À mon avis' goes at the beginning of the sentence and does not take 'que'. 'Il me semble que' is more formal and expresses an impression or supposition. After these expressions the verb is in the indicative (not subjunctive), unlike in Spanish.

concept_examples.text: Je pense que c'est une bonne idée.
concept_examples.translation: I think it's a good idea.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʒə pɑ̃s kə sɛ t‿yn bɔn ide/

concept_examples.text: Je trouve que ce film est magnifique.
concept_examples.translation: I find this movie magnificent.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʒə tʁuv kə sə film ɛ maɲifik/

concept_examples.text: À mon avis, il faut partir tôt.
concept_examples.translation: In my opinion, we have to leave early.
concept_examples.phonetic: /a mɔ̃ n‿avi, il fo paʁtiʁ to/

common_error.wrong: Je pense que c'est bien mais à mon avis que c'est compliqué.
common_error.correct: Je pense que c'est bien, mais à mon avis c'est compliqué.
common_error.correct_alt: Je pense que c'est bien, mais je trouve que c'est compliqué.
common_error.explanation: 'À mon avis' is never followed by 'que'. It is an opinion marker that directly introduces the sentence. The most frequent error is adding 'que' after it, by analogy with 'je pense que'. Remember: 'À mon avis + sentence without que'.

examples.original: Je pense que le français est difficile.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə pɑ̃s kə lə fʁɑ̃sɛ ɛ difisl/
examples.translation: I think French is difficult.
examples.note: 'Je pense que' is the most basic and frequent way to give an opinion. Verb in indicative after 'que'.

examples.original: À mon avis, Paris est très beau.
examples.phonetic: /a mɔ̃ n‿avi, paʁi ɛ tʁɛ bo/
examples.translation: In my opinion, Paris is very beautiful.
examples.note: 'À mon avis' does not take 'que'. It can be placed at the beginning or end of the sentence.

examples.original: Je trouve que ce restaurant est trop cher, mais la nourriture est excellente.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə tʁuv kə sə ʁɛstɔʁɑ̃ ɛ tʁo ʃɛʁ, mɛ la nuʁityʁ ɛ t‿ɛksɛlɑ̃t/
examples.translation: I find this restaurant too expensive, but the food is excellent.
examples.note: 'Je trouve que' adds a more personal and emotional nuance than 'je pense que'.

examples.original: Il me semble que nous avons un problème.
examples.phonetic: /il mə sɑ̃bl kə nu z‿avɔ̃ œ̃ pʁɔblɛm/
examples.translation: It seems to me that we have a problem.
examples.note: 'Il me semble que' expresses an impression or slight doubt; it is more formal and softer than 'je pense que'.

examples.original: À mon avis, il vaudrait mieux attendre, parce que je pense que la situation va changer.
examples.phonetic: /a mɔ̃ n‿avi, il vodʁɛ mjø atɑ̃dʁ, paʁs kə ʒə pɑ̃s kə la sitɥasjɔ̃ va ʃɑ̃ʒe/
examples.translation: In my opinion, it would be better to wait, because I think the situation is going to change.
examples.note: Combining 'à mon avis' with 'je pense que' in the same sentence is natural and very common.

examples.original: Je trouve que c'est intéressant, mais il me semble qu'il y a encore des problèmes à résoudre.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə tʁuv kə sɛ t‿ɛ̃teʁesɑ̃, mɛ il mə sɑ̃bl kil j‿a ɑ̃kɔʁ dɛ pʁɔblɛm a ʁezudʁ/
examples.translation: I find it interesting, but it seems to me that there are still problems to solve.
examples.note: Alternating opinion expressions enriches the discourse and avoids repetition.

vocabulary.translation: it seems to me that, I have the impression that
according to me, in my opinion

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Qu'est-ce que tu penses de ce nouveau film ?
dialogue.translation: What do you think of this new movie?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Je pense que c'est très bien réalisé. Et toi ?
dialogue.translation: I think it's very well made. And you?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Je trouve que c'est un peu long, mais à mon avis, l'histoire est excellente.
dialogue.translation: I find it a bit long, but in my opinion, the story is excellent.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Il me semble qu'il y a des scènes inutiles, mais dans l'ensemble je suis d'accord.
dialogue.translation: It seems to me that there are some useless scenes, but overall I agree.

title: Estar de acuerdo y en desacuerdo / Agreeing and disagreeing
bridge: In Spanish we say 'tienes razón', 'exacto', 'no estoy de acuerdo' or 'al contrario'. In French the equivalent expressions are 'C'est vrai', 'Exactement', 'Je ne suis pas d'accord' and 'Au contraire'. They are essential formulas for any conversation or debate.
rule: To show agreement use 'C'est vrai' (it's true), 'Exactement' (exactly), 'Tout à fait' (completely agree) or 'Je suis d'accord' (I agree). To show disagreement use 'Je ne suis pas d'accord' (I don't agree), 'Au contraire' (on the contrary) or 'Pas forcément' (not necessarily). Never say 'Je ne suis pas d'accord avec que' — always 'Je ne suis pas d'accord avec + noun' or 'Je ne suis pas d'accord' alone.

concept_examples.text: C'est vrai, tu as raison.
concept_examples.translation: It's true, you are right.

concept_examples.text: Je ne suis pas d'accord avec toi.
concept_examples.translation: I don't agree with you.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʒə nə sɥi pa dakɔʁ avɛk twa/

concept_examples.text: Au contraire, je pense que c'est une bonne idée.
concept_examples.translation: On the contrary, I think it's a good idea.
concept_examples.phonetic: /o kɔ̃tʁɛʁ, ʒə pɑ̃s kə sɛ t‿yn bɔn ide/

common_error.wrong: Je suis d'accord avec que tu dis.
common_error.correct: Je suis d'accord avec ce que tu dis.
common_error.explanation: In French you cannot say 'avec que'. To introduce what someone says you must use 'avec ce que' (with what). Many Spanish speakers literally translate 'de acuerdo con que' and omit the 'ce'. Remember: 'être d'accord avec ce que + phrase' or simply 'être d'accord avec + person/noun'.

examples.original: Oui, c'est vrai !
examples.phonetic: /wi, sɛ vʁɛ/
examples.translation: Yes, it's true!
examples.note: 'C'est vrai' is the simplest and most natural way to show agreement with what someone has just said.

examples.original: Non, je ne suis pas d'accord.
examples.phonetic: /nɔ̃, ʒə nə sɥi pa dakɔʁ/
examples.translation: No, I don't agree.
examples.note: Direct way to show disagreement. In French it can be used alone or followed by an explanation.

examples.original: Tout à fait, je pense exactement la même chose.
examples.phonetic: /tut‿a fɛ, ʒə pɑ̃s ɛɡzaktəmɑ̃ la mɛm ʃoz/
examples.translation: Absolutely, I think exactly the same thing.
examples.note: 'Tout à fait' is more emphatic than 'c'est vrai' and is equivalent to 'completely agree'.

examples.original: Au contraire, je trouve que c'est trop simple.
examples.phonetic: /o kɔ̃tʁɛʁ, ʒə tʁuv kə sɛ tʁo sɛ̃pl/
examples.translation: On the contrary, I find it too simple.
examples.note: 'Au contraire' directly contradicts what the other person has just said.

examples.original: Je suis d'accord avec ce que tu dis en général, mais pas forcément sur ce point.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə sɥi dakɔʁ avɛk sə kə ty di ɑ̃ ʒeneʁal, mɛ pa fɔʁsemɑ̃ syʁ sə pwɛ̃/
examples.translation: I agree with what you say in general, but not necessarily on this point.
examples.note: 'Pas forcément' (not necessarily) allows you to qualify disagreement without being blunt.

examples.original: C'est vrai dans une certaine mesure, cependant je ne suis pas entièrement d'accord.
examples.phonetic: /sɛ vʁɛ dɑ̃z‿yn sɛʁtɛn məzyʁ, səpɑ̃dɑ̃ ʒə nə sɥi pa ɑ̃tjɛʁmɑ̃ dakɔʁ/
examples.translation: It's true to a certain extent, however I don't entirely agree.
examples.note: 'Dans une certaine mesure' (to a certain extent) and 'cependant' (however) are connectors typical of formal register.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Je pense que les réseaux sociaux sont mauvais pour les jeunes.
dialogue.translation: I think social networks are bad for young people.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Je ne suis pas d'accord. À mon avis, ça dépend de l'usage.
dialogue.translation: I don't agree. In my opinion, it depends on the use.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: C'est vrai, pas forcément en tout cas.
dialogue.translation: It's true, not necessarily in any case.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Exactement ! Il faut apprendre à les utiliser correctement.
dialogue.translation: Exactly! We must learn to use them correctly.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Tout à fait, je suis d'accord avec ce que tu dis.
dialogue.translation: Absolutely, I agree with what you say.

title: Describir rutinas diarias / Describing daily routines
bridge: In Spanish we describe routines with reflexive verbs ('me levanto', 'me ducho') and sequence markers ('primero', 'después', 'finalmente'). In French it works exactly the same: reflexive verbs (je me lève, je me douche) and temporal markers (d'abord, ensuite, enfin). The logic is identical, only the form changes.
rule: Reflexive verbs in French are conjugated with the reflexive pronoun before the verb: je me lève, tu te lèves, il/elle se lève. To describe the order of actions use: 'd'abord' (first), 'ensuite' or 'puis' (then/after), 'enfin' (finally). These markers go at the beginning of the sentence followed by a comma.

concept_examples.text: Je me lève à sept heures.
concept_examples.translation: I get up at seven o'clock.

concept_examples.text: D'abord je me douche, ensuite je prends mon petit-déjeuner.
concept_examples.translation: First I shower, then I have breakfast.
concept_examples.phonetic: /dabɔʁ ʒə mə duʃ, ɑ̃sɥit ʒə pʁɑ̃ mɔ̃ pəti deʒœne/

concept_examples.text: Enfin, je me couche vers vingt-deux heures.
concept_examples.translation: Finally, I go to bed around ten in the evening.

common_error.wrong: Je me lève moi à sept heures et je lave moi les dents.
common_error.correct: Je me lève à sept heures et je me lave les dents.
common_error.explanation: The reflexive pronoun (me, te, se, nous, vous) always goes BEFORE the conjugated verb, never after. Saying 'je lave moi' is an incorrect calque from Spanish. The correct structure is always: subject + reflexive pronoun + verb. Example: je me lave, tu te lèves, il se couche.

examples.original: Je me réveille à six heures et demie.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə mə ʁevɛj a si z‿œʁ e dəmi/
examples.translation: I wake up at six thirty.
examples.note: 'Se réveiller' (to wake up) is the first step of the routine; do not confuse with 'se lever' (to get up), which comes after.

examples.original: D'abord, je me brosse les dents.
examples.phonetic: /dabɔʁ, ʒə mə bʁɔs lɛ dɑ̃/
examples.translation: First, I brush my teeth.
examples.note: 'D'abord' marks the first step of the sequence. Note that the body part uses the definite article (les dents), not a possessive.

examples.original: D'abord je me lève, ensuite je me douche, puis je m'habille.
examples.phonetic: /dabɔʁ ʒə mə lɛv, ɑ̃sɥit ʒə mə duʃ, pɥi ʒə m‿abij/
examples.translation: First I get up, then I shower, then I get dressed.
examples.note: 'Puis' and 'ensuite' are interchangeable. You can use one or the other to link actions in sequence.

examples.original: Le soir, je me repose un peu avant de me coucher.
examples.phonetic: /lə swaʁ, ʒə mə ʁəpoz œ̃ pø avɑ̃ də mə kuʃe/
examples.translation: In the evening, I rest a bit before going to bed.
examples.note: 'Avant de + infinitive' (before + infinitive) is a very useful construction for ordering actions.

examples.original: D'abord, je me lève à sept heures. Ensuite, je me douche et je m'habille. Puis, je prends mon petit-déjeuner. Enfin, je me prépare et je pars au travail.
examples.phonetic: /dabɔʁ, ʒə mə lɛv a sɛt‿œʁ. ɑ̃sɥit, ʒə mə duʃ e ʒə m‿abij. pɥi, ʒə pʁɑ̃ mɔ̃ pəti deʒœne. ɑ̃fɛ̃, ʒə mə pʁepaʁ e ʒə paʁ o tʁavaj/
examples.translation: First, I get up at seven. Then, I shower and get dressed. After that, I have breakfast. Finally, I get ready and leave for work.
examples.note: Complete description of the morning routine using the four markers in sequence. Each sentence can be independent.

examples.original: En général, je me couche vers vingt-trois heures, mais le week-end je me lève beaucoup plus tard.
examples.phonetic: /ɑ̃ ʒeneʁal, ʒə mə kuʃ vɛʁ vɛ̃tʁwa z‿œʁ, mɛ lə wikɛnd ʒə mə lɛv boku plys taʁ/
examples.translation: In general, I go to bed around eleven at night, but on weekends I get up much later.
examples.note: 'En général' and 'le week-end' allow contrasting the usual routine with exceptions.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Tu te lèves à quelle heure le matin ?
dialogue.translation: What time do you get up in the morning?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Je me lève à six heures et demie. D'abord je me douche, ensuite je m'habille.
dialogue.translation: I get up at six thirty. First I shower, then I get dressed.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Et tu prends le petit-déjeuner ?
dialogue.translation: And do you have breakfast?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Oui, puis je prends un café et des tartines. Enfin, je pars au travail vers huit heures.
dialogue.translation: Yes, then I have a coffee and some toast. Finally, I leave for work around eight.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Et le soir, tu te couches à quelle heure ?
dialogue.translation: And in the evening, what time do you go to bed?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: En général, je me couche vers vingt-deux heures trente.
dialogue.translation: In general, I go to bed around ten thirty.

title: Hablar de salud y síntomas / Talking about health and symptoms
bridge: In Spanish we say 'me duele...', 'tengo fiebre', 'me siento mal'. In French the equivalent structures are 'J'ai mal à...' (it hurts...), 'Je me sens...' (I feel...), 'J'ai de la fièvre' (I have a fever) and 'Je suis fatigué/e' (I am tired). The logic is very similar to Spanish, but with some differences in construction.
rule: To say that something hurts, use 'J'ai mal à + article + body part': J'ai mal à la tête (I have a headache), J'ai mal au ventre (I have a stomachache). 'À + le' contracts to 'au', and 'à + les' to 'aux'. To describe general state, use 'Je me sens + adjective' (I feel...) or 'Je suis + adjective' (I am...). For symptoms, use 'J'ai + noun': J'ai de la fièvre, J'ai un rhume.

concept_examples.text: J'ai mal à la gorge.
concept_examples.translation: I have a sore throat.

concept_examples.text: Je me sens très fatigué.
concept_examples.translation: I feel very tired.

concept_examples.text: J'ai de la fièvre depuis hier.
concept_examples.translation: I have had a fever since yesterday.

common_error.wrong: J'ai mal la tête. / Je suis mal à la tête.
common_error.explanation: The correct structure is 'avoir mal à + article + body part'. Do not omit the preposition 'à' nor use 'être' instead. 'J'ai mal la tête' (without 'à') and 'Je suis mal à la tête' are incorrect. Also remember the contractions: à + le = au (J'ai mal au dos), à + les = aux (J'ai mal aux pieds).

examples.original: J'ai mal à la tête.
examples.phonetic: /ʒɛ mal a la tɛt/
examples.translation: I have a headache.
examples.note: 'J'ai mal à + article + body part' is the fundamental structure. 'La tête' takes the feminine article.

examples.original: J'ai mal au ventre.
examples.phonetic: /ʒɛ mal o vɑ̃tʁ/
examples.translation: I have a stomachache.
examples.note: 'Au' is the contraction of 'à + le'. 'Le ventre' is masculine, so we use 'au'.

examples.original: J'ai de la fièvre et je me sens très faible.
examples.phonetic: /ʒɛ də la fjɛvʁ e ʒə mə sɑ̃ tʁɛ fɛbl/
examples.translation: I have a fever and I feel very weak.
examples.note: 'J'ai de la fièvre' (not 'j'ai fièvre' nor 'j'ai une fièvre'): fever in French always takes 'de la'.

examples.original: Je suis enrhumé(e) et j'ai mal à la gorge.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə sɥi ɑ̃ʁyme e ʒɛ mal a la ɡɔʁʒ/
examples.translation: I have a cold and a sore throat.
examples.note: 'Être enrhumé/e' (to have a cold) is the adjective for a cold. You can also say 'j'ai un rhume'.

examples.original: Je me sens mal depuis trois jours : j'ai de la fièvre, j'ai mal aux articulations et je suis épuisé(e).
examples.phonetic: /ʒə mə sɑ̃ mal dəpɥi tʁwa ʒuʁ : ʒɛ də la fjɛvʁ, ʒɛ mal o z‿aʁtikylasjɔ̃ e ʒə sɥi epɥize/
examples.translation: I have been feeling bad for three days: I have a fever, my joints hurt, and I am exhausted.
examples.note: 'Aux' is the contraction of 'à + les'. 'Épuisé/e' (exhausted) is stronger than 'fatigué/e' (tired).

examples.original: Docteur, j'ai des vertiges et je n'arrive pas à manger depuis ce matin.
examples.phonetic: /dɔktœʁ, ʒɛ dɛ vɛʁtiʒ e ʒə naʁiv pa a mɑ̃ʒe dəpɥi sə matɛ̃/
examples.translation: Doctor, I have been dizzy and I haven't been able to eat since this morning.
examples.note: 'Avoir des vertiges' (to be dizzy). 'Ne pas arriver à + infinitive' expresses inability or difficulty doing something.

vocabulary.translation: to hurt, to have pain in

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Tu n'as pas l'air bien. Ça va ?
dialogue.translation: You don't look well. Are you okay?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Non, je me sens vraiment mal. J'ai mal à la tête et j'ai de la fièvre.
dialogue.translation: No, I feel really bad. I have a headache and a fever.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Depuis quand ?
dialogue.translation: Since when?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Depuis hier soir. Je suis aussi très fatigué(e).
dialogue.translation: Since last night. I am also very tired.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Tu devrais aller chez le médecin. Tu veux que je t'accompagne ?
dialogue.translation: You should go to the doctor. Do you want me to come with you?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Oui, ce serait bien. Merci beaucoup.
dialogue.translation: Yes, that would be nice. Thank you very much.

title: Hacer peticiones y ofrecer ayuda / Making requests and offering help
bridge: In Spanish we ask for help with '¿Puedes...?', '¿Podría usted...?' and offer help with '¿Puedo ayudarte?', '¿Quieres que...?'. In French the equivalent structures are 'Tu peux...?' (informal), 'Est-ce que vous pouvez...?' (formal), 'Je peux vous aider?' and 'Voulez-vous que je...?'. The level of formality determines which formula to use.
rule: For informal requests use 'Tu peux + infinitive ?' (Can you...?). For formal requests or to strangers use 'Est-ce que vous pouvez + infinitive ?' or 'Pourriez-vous + infinitive ?' (conditional, more polite). To offer help use 'Je peux + infinitive ?' or 'Je peux vous/t'aider ?'. The structure 'Voulez-vous que je + subjunctive ?' is formal and expresses an offer to do something for someone.

concept_examples.text: Tu peux m'aider, s'il te plaît ?
concept_examples.translation: Can you help me, please?

concept_examples.text: Est-ce que vous pouvez répéter, s'il vous plaît ?
concept_examples.translation: Can you repeat, please?
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɛs kə vu puve ʁepete, sil vu plɛ/

concept_examples.text: Je peux vous aider ?
concept_examples.translation: Can I help you?

common_error.wrong: Pouvez-vous me dire l'heure, s'il te plaît ?
common_error.correct: Pouvez-vous me dire l'heure, s'il vous plaît ?
common_error.correct_alt: Tu peux me dire l'heure, s'il te plaît ?
common_error.explanation: The politeness formulas 'tu/vous' must be consistent throughout the sentence. If you use 'vous' (formal) with the verb (pouvez-vous), you must also use 's'il vous plaît', not 's'il te plaît'. Mixing the informal register (te plaît) with the formal (pouvez-vous) is a common mistake. Remember: 'vous' + 's'il vous plaît' / 'tu' + 's'il te plaît'.

examples.original: Tu peux fermer la fenêtre, s'il te plaît ?
examples.phonetic: /ty pø fɛʁme la fənɛtʁ, sil tə plɛ/
examples.translation: Can you close the window, please?
examples.note: 'Tu peux + infinitive' is the most direct and common way to ask something from someone you trust.

examples.original: Je peux t'aider à porter ça ?
examples.phonetic: /ʒə pø tɛde a pɔʁte sa/
examples.translation: Can I help you carry that?
examples.note: To offer help informally, just use 'Je peux + infinitive ?'. The rising intonation at the end indicates a question.

examples.original: Est-ce que vous pouvez parler plus lentement, s'il vous plaît ?
examples.phonetic: /ɛs kə vu puve paʁle plys lɑ̃tmɑ̃, sil vu plɛ/
examples.translation: Can you speak more slowly, please?
examples.note: 'Est-ce que vous pouvez' is the standard form for formal requests. 'S'il vous plaît' always accompanies 'vous'.

examples.original: Je peux vous aider à trouver quelque chose ?
examples.phonetic: /ʒə pø vu z‿ɛde a tʁuve kɛlkə ʃoz/
examples.translation: Can I help you find something?
examples.note: In shops, offices, or service contexts, this is the most common formula to offer help formally.

examples.original: Voulez-vous que je vous explique comment ça fonctionne ?
examples.phonetic: /vule vu kə ʒə vu z‿ɛksplik kɔmɑ̃ sa fɔ̃ksjɔn/
examples.translation: Would you like me to explain how it works?
examples.note: 'Voulez-vous que je + subjunctive ?' is a very polite formal offer. The subjunctive of 'expliquer' is 'explique', same as the present.

examples.original: Pourriez-vous me donner votre adresse e-mail, s'il vous plaît ?
examples.phonetic: /puʁje vu mə dɔne vɔtʁ adʁɛs imɛl, sil vu plɛ/
examples.translation: Could you give me your email address, please?
examples.note: 'Pourriez-vous' (conditional of pouvoir) is more formal and polite than 'est-ce que vous pouvez'. It is used in professional or very polite situations.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Excusez-moi, est-ce que vous pouvez m'aider ?
dialogue.translation: Excuse me, can you help me?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Bien sûr ! Je peux vous aider avec plaisir. Qu'est-ce que vous cherchez ?
dialogue.translation: Of course! I can help you with pleasure. What are you looking for?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Je cherche la rue Mouffetard. Vous pouvez m'indiquer la direction ?
dialogue.translation: I'm looking for Rue Mouffetard. Can you give me directions?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Voulez-vous que je vous montre sur la carte ?
dialogue.translation: Would you like me to show you on the map?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Oui, s'il vous plaît. C'est très gentil !
dialogue.translation: Yes, please. That's very kind!

title: Expresar habilidad y posibilidad / Expressing ability and possibility
bridge: In Spanish we say 'sé hablar francés' (learned ability), 'puedo venir' (possibility) and 'es posible que venga' (possibility with subjunctive). In French the distinction is similar: 'Je sais + infinitive' (to know how to do something), 'Je peux + infinitive' (can/possible) and 'Il est possible de + infinitive' or 'C'est possible que + subjunctive' (general or hypothetical possibility).
rule: Use 'Je sais + infinitive' to talk about acquired skills (Je sais nager = I know how to swim). Use 'Je peux + infinitive' to talk about possibility in a specific situation (Je peux venir = I can come). To talk about possibility in general, use 'Il est possible de + infinitive' (impersonal form) or 'C'est possible que + subjunctive present' (when the subject is different). The introduction of the subjunctive after 'C'est possible que' is a marker of A2+ level.

concept_examples.text: Je sais parler trois langues.
concept_examples.translation: I can speak three languages.

concept_examples.text: Je peux venir demain si tu veux.
concept_examples.translation: I can come tomorrow if you want.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʒə pø vəniʁ dəmɛ̃ si ty vø/

concept_examples.text: Il est possible de réserver en ligne.
concept_examples.translation: It is possible to book online.
concept_examples.phonetic: /il ɛ pɔsibl də ʁezɛʁve ɑ̃ liɲ/

common_error.wrong: Je sais venir demain. / Je peux nager depuis l'enfance.
common_error.correct: Je peux venir demain. / Je sais nager depuis l'enfance.
common_error.explanation: 'Savoir + infinitive' expresses a learned and lasting ability (to know how to do something). 'Pouvoir + infinitive' expresses possibility or permission in a specific situation. They are not interchangeable: 'Je sais venir' makes no sense (coming is not a learned ability), and 'je peux nager depuis l'enfance' sounds odd because swimming is a skill. The distinction between 'saber' and 'poder' exists in French just as in Spanish.

examples.original: Je sais cuisiner des pâtes.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə sɛ kɥizine dɛ pat/
examples.translation: I know how to cook pasta.
examples.note: 'Savoir + infinitive' = to have the ability to do something. It is a skill that has been learned.

examples.original: Je ne sais pas conduire.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə nə sɛ pa kɔ̃dɥiʁ/
examples.translation: I don't know how to drive.
examples.note: The negation of 'je sais' is 'je ne sais pas'. Very common to express one's limitations without drama.

examples.original: Je peux t'aider à déménager ce week-end.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə pø tɛde a demenaʒe sə wikɛnd/
examples.translation: I can help you move this weekend.
examples.note: 'Je peux + infinitive' expresses availability or possibility in a specific context, not a permanent ability.

examples.original: Il est possible de payer par carte dans ce magasin.
examples.phonetic: /il ɛ pɔsibl də peje paʁ kaʁt dɑ̃ sə maɡazɛ̃/
examples.translation: It is possible to pay by card in this store.
examples.note: 'Il est possible de + infinitive' is the impersonal construction to say that something is possible in general. It does not refer to any specific subject.

examples.original: C'est possible qu'il vienne ce soir, mais je ne suis pas sûr.
examples.phonetic: /sɛ pɔsibl kil vjɛn sə swaʁ, mɛ ʒə nə sɥi pa syʁ/
examples.translation: It's possible that he comes tonight, but I'm not sure.
examples.note: 'C'est possible que + subjunctive' introduces uncertainty about something that could happen. 'Vienne' is the subjunctive of 'venir': il vienne.

examples.original: Je sais que je peux réussir, mais il est possible que j'aie besoin d'aide.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə sɛ kə ʒə pø ʁeysiʁ, mɛ il ɛ pɔsibl kə ʒɛ bəzwɛ̃ dɛd/
examples.translation: I know I can succeed, but it's possible that I need help.
examples.note: 'J'aie besoin' is the subjunctive of 'avoir' (that I have/need). Note how in a single sentence 'je sais', 'je peux' and 'il est possible que + subjunctive' coexist.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Tu sais faire du vélo ?
dialogue.translation: Do you know how to ride a bike?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Oui, je sais faire du vélo depuis que j'ai six ans. Et toi, tu sais nager ?
dialogue.translation: Yes, I've known how to ride a bike since I was six. And you, do you know how to swim?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Oui, mais je ne nage pas très bien. Je peux nager en piscine, mais pas en mer.
dialogue.translation: Yes, but I don't swim very well. I can swim in a pool, but not in the sea.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: C'est possible que tu aies peur des vagues ?
dialogue.translation: Is it possible that you're afraid of waves?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Peut-être ! Il est possible de prendre des cours de natation pour adultes ici ?
dialogue.translation: Maybe! Is it possible to take adult swimming lessons here?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Oui, je suis sûr que tu peux t'inscrire à la piscine municipale.
dialogue.translation: Yes, I'm sure you can sign up at the municipal pool.

title: Hablar del tiempo meteorológico / Talking about the weather
bridge: In Spanish we say 'hace frío', 'llueve', '¿qué tiempo hace?'. In French the equivalent structures are 'Il fait froid', 'Il pleut', 'Quel temps fait-il?'. There is a key difference: in French, the impersonal verb 'il fait' (literally 'it makes') is almost always used for the weather, or specific verbs like 'il pleut' (it rains) and 'il neige' (it snows). The subject is always impersonal 'il', never 'elle' or 'ça' in standard register.
rule: Use 'Il fait + adjective' to describe general weather: Il fait beau (it's nice weather), Il fait chaud (it's hot), Il fait froid (it's cold), Il fait mauvais (it's bad weather). For rain and snow, use specific verbs: Il pleut (it's raining), Il neige (it's snowing). To ask about the weather, use 'Quel temps fait-il?' (What's the weather like?). For forecasts, use 'La météo prévoit + noun/infinitive' (the weather forecast announces...) or 'Il va + infinitive' with the near future.

concept_examples.text: Il fait beau aujourd'hui.
concept_examples.translation: It's nice weather today.

concept_examples.text: Il pleut depuis ce matin.
concept_examples.translation: It's been raining since this morning.

concept_examples.text: Quel temps fait-il demain ?
concept_examples.translation: What's the weather like tomorrow?

common_error.wrong: Il fait pleut. / Il fait neige. / Ça fait froid.
common_error.correct: Il pleut. / Il neige. / Il fait froid.
common_error.explanation: The verbs 'pleuvoir' (to rain) and 'neiger' (to snow) are complete impersonal verbs: they are conjugated on their own as 'il pleut' and 'il neige', without adding 'fait'. Do not combine 'il fait' with them. Also, never use 'ça fait' instead of 'il fait' for the weather: 'ça fait froid' is not correct in this context. The impersonal subject for weather is always 'il'.

levels.label: Décrire le temps du jour
levels.translation: Describing the weather of the day

examples.original: Il fait beau et il fait chaud.
examples.phonetic: /il fɛ bo e il fɛ ʃo/
examples.translation: It's nice weather and it's hot.
examples.note: 'Il fait beau' (nice weather) and 'il fait chaud' (hot) are the most basic expressions. Always 'il fait + adjective'.

examples.original: Il fait froid ce matin.
examples.phonetic: /il fɛ fʁwa sə matɛ̃/
examples.translation: It's cold this morning.
examples.note: 'Ce matin' (this morning) adds temporal precision. 'Il fait froid' is the standard form, never 'il est froid'.

examples.original: Il pleut à verse, prends un parapluie !
examples.phonetic: /il plø a vɛʁs, pʁɑ̃ z‿œ̃ paʁaplɥi/
examples.translation: It's pouring rain, take an umbrella!
examples.note: 'Pleuvoir à verse' (to pour) intensifies 'il pleut'. 'Un parapluie' is the umbrella.

examples.original: Il y a du vent et des nuages.
examples.phonetic: /il j‿a dy vɑ̃ e dɛ nɥaʒ/
examples.translation: There is wind and clouds.
examples.note: 'Il y a + noun' is another frequent way to describe weather phenomena: du vent (wind), des nuages (clouds), du brouillard (fog), du soleil (sun).

examples.original: La météo prévoit des orages pour cet après-midi.
examples.phonetic: /la meteo pʁevwa dɛ z‿ɔʁaʒ puʁ sɛt apʁɛmidi/
examples.translation: The weather forecast predicts storms for this afternoon.
examples.note: 'La météo prévoit + noun' is the formal expression for talking about forecasts. 'Des orages' (storms) is the plural of 'un orage'.

examples.original: D'après la météo, il va neiger demain matin et les températures vont descendre en dessous de zéro.
examples.phonetic: /dapʁɛ la meteo, il va nɛʒe dəmɛ̃ matɛ̃ e lɛ tɑ̃peʁatyʁ vɔ̃ desɑ̃dʁ ɑ̃ dəsu də zeʁo/
examples.translation: According to the forecast, it will snow tomorrow morning and temperatures will drop below zero.
examples.note: 'D'après la météo' (according to the weather forecast) introduces forecast information. 'En dessous de zéro' (below zero) is the expression for talking about negative temperatures.

vocabulary.word: il y a du soleil / vent / brouillard

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Quel temps fait-il aujourd'hui ?
dialogue.translation: What's the weather like today?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Il fait assez froid et il y a des nuages. Je crois qu'il va pleuvoir.
dialogue.translation: It's quite cold and there are clouds. I think it's going to rain.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Ah bon ? Et pour le week-end, tu sais ce que dit la météo ?
dialogue.translation: Oh really? And for the weekend, do you know what the forecast says?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: La météo prévoit du soleil samedi, mais il va faire encore froid.
dialogue.translation: The forecast predicts sun on Saturday, but it will still be cold.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Tant mieux ! J'avais prévu une promenade. Je prends quand même un manteau.
dialogue.translation: Good! I had planned a walk. I'll take a coat anyway.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Bonne idée ! Et prends ton parapluie, on ne sait jamais avec ce temps.
dialogue.translation: Good idea! And take your umbrella, you never know with this weather.

title: Parler de la météo / Talking about the weather
bridge: In Spanish, to talk about the weather we use the verb 'hacer' (hace calor, hace frío) or 'hay' (hay niebla). In French, the verb 'faire' is mainly used (il fait chaud, il fait froid) and also 'il y a' (il y a du brouillard). Note: in French, the subject 'il' (impersonal) is always required, whereas in Spanish we do not say 'él hace calor'. Furthermore, phenomena like raining or snowing are expressed with impersonal verbs: 'il pleut', 'il neige', which in Spanish are 'llueve' and 'nieva'.
rule: To talk about the weather in French at A2 level: 1) With 'faire' to describe the general state: il fait beau (it's nice weather), il fait mauvais (it's bad weather), il fait chaud (it's hot), il fait froid (it's cold), il fait du vent (it's windy), il fait du soleil (it's sunny). 2) With 'il y a' for phenomena: il y a du brouillard (there is fog), il y a des nuages (there are clouds). 3) With impersonal verbs for precipitation: il pleut (it's raining), il neige (it's snowing), il grêle (it's hailing). 4) For temperatures: il fait 20 degrés (it's 20 degrees) or il fait moins cinq (it's minus five). Remember that 'il' is mandatory, it cannot be omitted. In questions: Quel temps fait-il ? (What's the weather like?) and for the near future: il va pleuvoir (it's going to rain), il va faire froid (it's going to be cold).

concept_examples.text: Quel temps fait-il aujourd'hui ?
concept_examples.translation: What's the weather like today?

concept_examples.text: Il fait beau et il fait chaud.
concept_examples.translation: It's nice weather and it's hot.
concept_examples.phonetic: /il fɛ bo e il fɛ ʃo/

concept_examples.text: Il pleut beaucoup en automne.
concept_examples.translation: It rains a lot in autumn.

concept_examples.text: Il y a du vent sur la côte.
concept_examples.translation: It's windy on the coast.
concept_examples.phonetic: /il j a dy vɑ̃ syʁ la kot/

common_error.correct_alt: Il fait de la pluie. (less common)
common_error.explanation: The error comes from literally translating 'hace lluvia' from Spanish. In French, rain is not expressed with 'faire' + noun, but with the impersonal verb 'pleuvoir'. Remember: for weather phenomena that are actions, use impersonal verbs (il pleut, il neige, il gèle) instead of 'faire'.

examples.original: Il fait beau aujourd'hui.
examples.phonetic: /il fɛ bo o.ʒur.dɥi/
examples.translation: It's nice weather today.
examples.note: Use 'il fait' + adjective to describe the general weather. 'Beau' means 'good' in this context.

examples.original: Il fait mauvais.
examples.phonetic: /il fɛ mɔ.vɛ/
examples.translation: It's bad weather.
examples.note: 'Mauvais' is the opposite of 'beau'. Be careful with the pronunciation of the final 's': it is not pronounced.

examples.original: Il fait froid en hiver.
examples.phonetic: /il fɛ fʁwa ɑ̃ i.vɛʁ/
examples.translation: It's cold in winter.
examples.note: Remember that 'en' + season (without article) for 'in winter'. In Spanish we say 'en invierno', but in French it is 'en hiver'.

examples.original: Il pleut depuis ce matin.
examples.phonetic: /il plø də.pɥi sə ma.tɛ̃/
examples.translation: It has been raining since this morning.
examples.note: Note the use of the present tense 'il pleut' (it's raining). 'Depuis' expresses duration, similar to 'since' in Spanish.

examples.original: Il neige dans les montagnes.
examples.phonetic: /il nɛʒ dɑ̃ le mɔ̃.taɲ/
examples.translation: It's snowing in the mountains.
examples.note: The verb 'neiger' is only used in the impersonal third person singular. Do not say 'il neige des flocons' (that would be incorrect).

examples.original: Il y a du brouillard.
examples.phonetic: /il j a dy bʁu.jaʁ/
examples.translation: There is fog.
examples.note: For 'there is' with uncountable nouns, use 'il y a du/de la/des'. Fog is 'du brouillard' (masculine).

examples.original: Il fait du vent aujourd'hui.
examples.phonetic: /il fɛ dy vɑ̃ o.ʒur.dɥi/
examples.translation: It's windy today.
examples.note: With 'vent' we use 'faire' + 'du', not 'il y a'. It's an exception: 'il fait du vent' (literally 'it makes wind').

examples.original: Quelle température fait-il ?
examples.phonetic: /kɛl tɑ̃.pe.ʁa.tyʁ fɛ.til/
examples.translation: What's the temperature?
examples.note: Common question. The inversion 'fait-il' is used in formal style. Colloquially, you can also say 'Il fait quelle température ?'

examples.original: Il fait vingt degrés.
examples.phonetic: /il fɛ vɛ̃ də.ɡʁe/
examples.translation: It's twenty degrees.
examples.note: For temperatures, use 'faire' + number + 'degrés'. In Spanish we say 'hace 20 grados', same structure.

examples.original: Demain, il va pleuvoir.
examples.phonetic: /də.mɛ̃ il va plø.vwaʁ/
examples.translation: Tomorrow it's going to rain.
examples.note: For the near future, use 'aller' + infinitive: 'il va pleuvoir'. Similar to Spanish 'ir a + infinitive'.

examples.original: Il va faire froid ce week-end.
examples.phonetic: /il va fɛʁ fʁwa sə wi.kɛnd/
examples.translation: It's going to be cold this weekend.
examples.note: Combine 'il va faire' + adjective. 'Ce week-end' is used the same as in Spanish, although 'le week-end' is also said.
